rows.question: How does housing lottery priority differ for rising sophomores versus juniors and seniors?

results.text:
On the housing lottery

The housing lottery is not random in the way most people assume. Rising sophomores get a number drawn at random, but juniors and seniors are ordered by accumulated credit hours first, and only tie-break randomly. That means a senior who took summer courses reliably beats a senior who didn't. Numbers come out the second week of March and selection runs over four evenings.
results.label: admin_housing_lottery.txt#0

results.text:
Tamsin Court — what it's actually like

I lived here my sophomore year. Built 2021. Rooms are studio apartments with private kitchen and bathroom.

The good: the most independent housing on campus, and the only option with a full kitchen.

The bad: the most expensive tier by a wide margin, and isolating if you're new.
results.label: housing_tamsin_court.txt#0

results.text:
STAT 150 Applied Statistics — assessment

Three equally weighted midterms, no final. No curve, but the lowest midterm is dropped.

The dropped midterm makes the first one low-stakes; use it to learn the format.
results.label: course_stat_150_exams.txt#0

results.text:
Registration and your adviser

You need an adviser hold lifted before you can register, and advisers get busy in the week before registration opens. Book two weeks out.

Registration times are staggered by credit hours, same as the housing lottery. Popular courses fill in the first two days.

rows.question: What are the separate wash and dry prices in Morrow House, and which payment methods work?

results.text:
Laundry in Morrow House

Machines take $1.50 wash, $1.25 dry, coin or card. There are eight washers and six dryers for the building, which is the wrong ratio and means the dryers back up on Sunday evenings.

Best time to do laundry here is Tuesday or Wednesday morning. Sunday after 6pm you will wait.

rows.question: How long is the Kestrel Commons wait between 12:15 and 1:00, and before 11:45?

results.text:
Re: Kestrel Commons

Adding to what people have said about Kestrel Commons. The wait figure of 20 to 25 minutes between 12:15 and 1:00 matches what I've seen. If you're trying to eat between classes, go before 11:45 and it's a different building entirely.

Also worth saying: the salad bar wilts after 1:30. Nobody tells you this at orientation.

rows.question: When does the library close during term versus reading week?

results.text:
Library hours and where to actually sit

Open until 2am during term, until 10pm during reading week, which is backwards and catches everyone out every single year.

Third floor is silent and enforced. Second floor is quiet in theory. The basement has the only outlets at every seat and is therefore full from about 10am.
results.label: study_library_hours.txt#0

results.text:
Noise levels in Calder Annexe

Asked about this a lot so writing it down. Depends entirely on your cluster; there's no building-wide pattern.

If you're someone who needs quiet to work, the library is open until 2am during term and that's what most people in this building end up doing.
results.label: housing_calder_annexe_noise.txt#0

results.text:
On the library holds

You can place a hold on a checked-out book and it usually arrives in two to three days. What isn't advertised: the interlibrary system covers eleven other institutions and requests through it take about a week but almost never fail.
results.label: admin_library_holds.txt#0

The library holds one copy of most required texts on two-hour reserve. For courses where the text is used constantly that isn't enough, but for the reading-light courses it's genuinely all you need.
